source_context_translations.translation: Too much talk leads to repeated failure; it is better to hold to the center.
The valley spirit does not die; this is called the mysterious female.
The gate of the mysterious female is called the root of Heaven and Earth.
It is continuous and seems to endure, yet its use is never exhausted.
Heaven is long-lasting; Earth is enduring.
Heaven and Earth are able to last long and endure because they do not live for themselves,
Therefore the sage puts himself behind, and yet comes first; he sets himself aside, and yet survives.
Is it not because he is without selfishness? Therefore he is able to realize his own interests.
The highest goodness is like water.
Water benefits the ten thousand things and does not contend, dwelling in places that others dislike,

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A large amount or degree; in this context, excessive quantity of speech.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often implies excess or an undesirable amount when used of speech or action.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A countable quantity or numeral value.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used for numerical quantity rather than frequency.
Sentence Translations (English): The number does not reach ten.
He asked the historian for the tally.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): At frequent intervals or on many occasions, not just in number but in recurrence.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this kind of text it marks repeated occurrence, not numerical counting.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Lacking resources or in a low, needy condition.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes material poverty or a lowly condition.
Sentence Translations (English): Though the gentleman is poor, his will is not bent.
He lived in poverty and held to himself.
A noble man does not resent poverty.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To reach a limit and fail to continue; to run out of effectiveness, possibilities, or resources.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests final depletion or getting stuck at a limit.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension
contextual_sense.Translation (English): come to an end; be exhausted

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Used to compare two alternatives and say that the first is inferior to the second in fitness or desirability.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A judgment of comparative preference, not merely factual inequality.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To watch over something and keep it safe from harm or loss.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Focuses on defense or custody rather than steadfast adherence.
Sentence Translations (English): They guarded the city and waited for relief.
Guard it and do not let it be lost.
The troops were few but could hold the defense.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To maintain or adhere to a principle, position, or state.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means steady adherence rather than physical guarding.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The central part of something in space or position.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used of physical or positional center.
Sentence Translations (English): He lived in the middle of the city.
There is a high terrace in the center.
Look to the center and act.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A central, balanced, or middle position, especially the proper course that avoids extremes.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is not merely spatial middle, but the balanced norm of conduct or being.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A mysterious generative power imagined as dwelling in or like a valley, and associated with enduring fertility.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A Daoist cosmological image, not a literal spirit of an actual valley.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): No longer living; having died.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes the state of having ceased to live.
Sentence Translations (English): A dead horse still has bones.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To cease living; to be no longer alive.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Neutral basic verb for death, without special literary elevation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A demonstrative referring to something present, already mentioned, or about to be identified.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used for pointing back to a specific thing or statement.
Sentence Translations (English): This and that are not yet clear.
It rained hard on that day.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A copular or demonstrative identification introducing an explanation or naming something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it introduces an explanatory identification, not a yes/no answer.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A darkly hidden feminine source or generative principle, used as a Daoist cosmological name.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A technical Daoist image of fecund origin, not ordinary reference to a woman.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The underground part of a plant.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Literal botanical sense.
Sentence Translations (English): Transplant the roots into the courtyard.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The underlying base or origin from which something grows, begins, or depends.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this phrase it means ultimate source rather than a plant root alone.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Extended in a soft, thin, or uninterrupted way, without obvious break or end.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests a subtle, scarcely perceptible continuity.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a condition or supposition.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Conditional use, common in classical prose.
Sentence Translations (English): If he does not come, what then?
If one can turn back on oneself, that is good.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks resemblance or conjectural comparison: something appears to be or seems like another state.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it introduces an appearance or likeness, not a condition.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Applying steady effort and labor.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes energetic application, especially in service or study.
Sentence Translations (English): If one studies without diligence, how can one succeed?
He was diligent in affairs of state.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To use up strength or resources, or to cause something to become exhausted.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests depletion through use or effort, not simple diligence.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The visible expanse above the earth.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Literal physical sky rather than cosmological Heaven.
Sentence Translations (English): He looked up and saw the sky.
The sky is about to darken.
Clouds came out in the sky.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The sky or the celestial realm, often as a cosmic power or order in classical thought.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often carries cosmological force, not just the visible sky.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To become longer, larger, or more extended.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A separate reading with the sense of increase or growth.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Continuing for a great length of time; enduring without ending soon.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it describes durability or continuance, not simple spatial length.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The surface of the earth or a piece of land.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Physical ground or territory rather than cosmic Earth.
Sentence Translations (English): The ground was flat as a palm.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The terrestrial world, the land, or the earthly realm in cosmic pairing with Heaven.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Cosmological counterpart to Heaven, not merely soil.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Continuing over an extended time, without quick termination.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Emphasizes duration and staying power.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A location or point where something is situated or happens.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Literal spatial sense.
Sentence Translations (English): He had no fixed place to live.
Wherever he directed himself, all went smoothly.
What he had not yet seen.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces the basis, method, or explanation for something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this construction it forms an explanatory relative phrase, not a concrete place noun.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension
contextual_sense.Translation (English): the means by which; the reason why

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The power or competence to do something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Refers to capacity as a quality or a person who possesses it.
Sentence Translations (English): This is not within human ability.
Those who are capable are employed.
He is versatile and makes few mistakes.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To have the capacity, power, or possibility to do something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks capability or effective power, not mere permission.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Used to intensify a statement or add an emphatic further point.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often strengthens what follows rather than merely joining clauses.
Sentence Translations (English): Its momentum is even more vigorous.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Adds another element or parallel case, often with a sense of further inclusion.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it links two enduring qualities and can suggest ‘even’ or ‘moreover’ depending on context.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates a starting point or source.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Marks origin or starting point.
Sentence Translations (English): It has been so since ancient times.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks that an action or state originates from oneself rather than from others or outside causes.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means self-generated or self-directed, not the standalone noun 'self.'
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Following in time, sequence, or order.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Temporal or ordinal sense.
Sentence Translations (English): Only afterward did he know it.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To take a rear or secondary position, yielding precedence to others.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): An intentional act of self-effacement, not merely being later in time.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The physical frame of a person or animal.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Literal bodily sense.
Sentence Translations (English): He entered in person through the gate.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The physical person, and by extension oneself as an embodied being.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Can point either to the bodily self or the person as a whole; here it is the person in relation to advancement or preservation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Outside a space, boundary, or group.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Spatial sense of being external.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To place beyond concern or to treat as secondary, as when one does not make personal advantage central.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): This is a deliberate self-distancing, not simple physical exteriority.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Concern for one's own advantage or advantage for one’s own side rather than for the whole.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it names self-regarding partiality, contrasted with impartiality or non-selfing.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Belonging to an individual rather than to the public or state.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Not public or official.
Sentence Translations (English): Do not discuss his private affairs.
The private gate is already closed.
Private feelings are hard to exhaust.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): What belongs to or benefits oneself rather than the public, shared, or impartial good.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often contrasts with public or impartial concerns; here it is the object being achieved or preserved.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): In a higher position or location.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Spatial or positional sense.
Sentence Translations (English): The book was placed on the table.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): At the top or in the most excellent position.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this phrase it means the highest grade of goodness, not spatial above.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The liquid substance that flows, nourishes, and takes the shape of its container.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Standard natural substance, here used as a moral and cosmological model.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having a sharp edge or acute cutting power.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concrete physical sharpness.
Sentence Translations (English): A sharp tool may be used.
A stone can be worn to sharpness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To provide advantage, help, or practical benefit to something or someone.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this context it emphasizes beneficial action rather than profit-making.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, inherited Laozi base text in the Wang Bi recension
